event: Weekly Market Review
title: Weekly Market Review
text:
BOTTOM LINE — Broad rebound week; semis and silver led, defensives lagged.
The S&P's best week in 19 months came from an oversold snapback after a sharp tech decline, with SOXX +8.65% leading and cyclicals (XLB, XLI) outrunning defensives (XLE, XLU). Money went into risk (XLF +$1,174mm, XLK +$708mm) and out of gold (GLD -$2,409mm) and health care (XLV -$1,480mm). Strength was broad, not narrow — 407 of 502 S&P names rose.

INDICES — QQQ +6.99%, IWM +6.69%, SPY +5.58%, DIA +5.51%.
Large beat small by 0.30pp (large +6.99% vs small +6.69%) — an AI-led, not broadening, tape. VIX sits at 26.8, still above its 23.6 20-day average despite the weekly VIX-futures drop (VIXY -7.77% Friday). Silver was the week's big cross-asset move, SLV +6.57% (and +6.20% Friday); gold added 3.57% while long Treasuries lagged (TLT -1.18% Friday). SPY and QQQ both remain BELOW their 200-day MAs.

SECTORS & ROTATION — XLB Materials +7.88%, XLK Technology +7.48%, XLC Comm Svcs +7.45%, XLY Cons Disc +6.68%, XLI Industrials +5.88%, XLF Financials +4.75%, XLRE Real Estate +3.96%, XLV Health Care +3.93%, XLP Staples +2.45%, XLU Utilities +2.44%, XLE Energy +1.92%.
Top industries: SILJ +16.95% and GDX +15.76%; bottom: USO -1.33% and UNG -6.82%. Flows confirm the rotation — financials and tech pulled in 96th- and 94th-percentile inflows while energy and health care bled at the 0th percentile. Rotation-state: broad risk-on.

DRIVERS — Semis and precious metals carried the tape: SOXX +8.65%, SLV +6.57%, with miners (SILJ, GDX) the strongest industries, while energy (XLE +1.92%) and nat gas (UNG -6.82%) lagged on a soft crude tape (USO +1.08% industry, oil off Friday). Volume was thin across the holiday week — advancing index volume ran 0.9x avg (SOXX, SLV) with breadth an unusually clean 81% up and a 9.12 up/down volume ratio, yet only 63% of names above their 50-day. The driver was mechanical: an oversold bounce off a deep 20-day drawdown (XLK -15.15%, SOXX -73.91% 20d), not a fresh catalyst. Released macro was mixed — Q3 GDP revised up to 4.3% (fc 3.5%) and new home sales 70.1 (fc 65) beat, while durable goods +0.2% missed and core PCE YoY ran 3.3% (fc 3.2%).

WHAT'S NEXT — Watch whether the bounce holds above the 200-day: SPY and QQQ are still beneath theirs, so a failure to reclaim keeps the tape rangebound. IV is rich into next week — QQQ ATM 28.9%, SLV 53.7% — with SPY maxpain 719 vs GEX flip 724, a setup for pinning or a vol crush. ISM Manufacturing (fc 55), JOLTs (fc 745) and the Dec 9 FOMC are the live catalysts; rate-hike odds for January 2027 sit at 54% on Polymarket.
